# RUN 5 — publish protocol (build, pointer, digests, client)

**Source of truth:** `ARCHITECTURE.md` §5.5 (entire), §12.1 (digest + inventory envelope), §13.5 (rollback semantics), §14 (job split — files only this run), §17 P1 gates. Staging mode (P1): **no attestations** — the trust boundary is the private repo ACL; every attestation call site must exist as a clean seam (`attestation.py` with a `StagingNoop` implementation + interface documented for the P2 sigstore implementation).

## Scope (owns)

`src/populus/publish/__init__.py`, `publish/build.py`, `publish/manifest.py`, `publish/pointer.py`, `publish/digests.py`, `publish/inventory.py`, `publish/attestation.py`, `src/populus/client/__init__.py`, `client/snapshot.py` (consumer protocol + pointer state machine), `tests/test_publish.py`, `tests/test_pointer_state.py`, `tests/test_digests.py`, `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, `.github/workflows/record-sign.yml`, `scripts/monitor.py` (mini heartbeat, §13.2), `docs/runbooks/rollback.md`, `docs/runbooks/disaster-recovery.md`. Wire `populus build/publish/verify`.

## Requirements

1. **Build** (§5.5): `build_id = YYYYMMDD.N` (UTC; N = same-day seq, injected clock for tests — **no wall-clock reads in library code paths that tests cover**); assemble build-scoped artifacts (congress.db snapshot, feed.json, per-entity JSON slices minimal set, stats.json) under `builds/<build_id>/`; manifest exactly per the §5.5 example: `schema_version`, `client_compat` (PEP 440 string), `deprecation`, `normalization_version`, `digest_projection_version`, watermarks, artifacts[] with sha256/bytes/path-or-url/license_ids, `previous_build_id`.
2. **Logical digest** (§5.5, versioned projection v1): allowlist — `ingest_runs` excluded entirely; `members`, `member_aliases`, `filings`, `transactions` minus `filings.ingested_at`; RFC 8785 rows, PK-sorted, `T:<table>\n` framing; **test: two independent builds of the same raw inputs yield identical `logical_digest`** (P1 gate).
3. **Pointer** (§5.5): schema (`pointer_version` monotonic, `issued_at`, `expires_at` +7d, `build_id`, `manifest_path`, `manifest_sha256`); **four-way state machine with universal preconditions FIRST** (schema validity, expiry & future-issuance vs current clock every refresh, attestation via the seam): lower⇒replay-reject · equal+same-bytes⇒idempotent accept · equal+diff⇒equivocation alarm · higher⇒verify manifest_sha256→install→atomically persist `(version, sha256)` tuple. Client cache layout `~/.cache/populus/<module>/<build_id>/` + temp-verify-rename; prior cache untouched on any failure.
4. **Publication order** (§5.5 P1 sequence): assets → manifest commit → pointer last, into a **local `populus-data` working tree** (`--data-repo PATH`, default `../populus-data`); `populus publish` refuses partial builds (`populus verify` gate: recompute all hashes + logical digests + pointer/manifest consistency). Release-asset abstraction: local-dir backend now, `gh release` backend behind the same interface (not exercised in tests). **Recovery contract (precise — supersedes any earlier "same build_id at every boundary" wording):** automatic recovery completes the **same `build_id` from the first durably-recoverable object (the uploaded+verified recovery journal) onward**; the earlier pre-journal boundaries create **no durably-recoverable state** and are handled by **safe-refuse + rebuild** (owner-accepted, DR-5-driven — see Tech Debt). This is by-design, not a broken promise.
5. **Inventory + dist digest** (§12.1): implement `digests.dist_digest(tree)` (exact framing: path`\0`len`\0`sha256hex`\n`, bytewise path sort, regular files only — symlink/non-regular ⇒ hard error) and `inventory.py` (RFC 8785 `inventory.json` sibling, `inventory_digest`) — used by the dashboard deploy later; tested with fixture trees incl. rejection cases.
6. **Fixtures** (§17 P1/P2 drills as tests): pointer fixtures (g) equal-but-expired fails refresh with stale status, (h) future-issued rejected, (i) state-loss bootstrap accepts one unexpired pointer (client) while a `monitor_mode=True` variant fails closed; equivocation alarm; replay reject; authorized rollback (higher version→older build) accepted; hash-verification fixture — a tampered artifact byte is detected and the prior cache retained.
7. **Workflow files** (§14, files only, not armed): `publish.yml` (permissions blocks per §14, concurrency group `data-publish`, staging = private-repo aware), `record-sign.yml` (reusable workflow shape, Pages-Read token env name, no-op guard until P3), `scripts/monitor.py` implementing §13.2 (pointer state machine w/ durable tuple on disk, manifest-listed stats fetch, fail-closed on missing/corrupt tuple, immutable-setting check stub).

## Acceptance

`uv run pytest -q` green (incl. two-build logical-digest reproducibility and every pointer fixture); `populus build && populus publish --data-repo ../populus-data && populus verify --data-repo ../populus-data` succeeds end-to-end against a real ingested DB; a second publish bumps `pointer_version` and an unchanged re-poll is an idempotent accept.

**Tests Run:** `uv run pytest -q` → **918 passing** (whole repo; RUN-5 surface + all prior runs).

## Dev Notes — Tech Debt

**TD (owner-accepted 2026-07-23) — pre-draft crash boundary is benign, not same-build_id recoverable.** Precise contract: automatic recovery **completes the same `build_id` from the first durably-recoverable object (the uploaded+verified recovery journal) onward** (R25/R31/R35); the earlier boundaries **create no durably-recoverable state** and are handled by **safe-refuse + rebuild** (owner-accepted, DR-5-driven) — this is by-design, not a broken "completes at every boundary" promise. Before the first remote mutation (`build` has staged `.staging/<build_id>/journal.json`, `publish` has not yet created the draft), **no durable remote or committed state exists**, so a crash strands nothing: a fresh runner rebuilds from source (the ingested `congress.db` is regenerable via the §13.5 re-ingest path) and publishes normally; `next_build_id` burns the interrupted id. Committing the recovery journal to git to cover this pre-draft window was **considered and explicitly rejected**: the journal inlines `congress.db` as base64 (~35 MB/build → ~1 GB/month permanently in git history), which would regress **DR-5 / §13.4** (SQLite snapshots are Release assets precisely to keep the data repo out of git-bloat, under the >1 GB migration trigger). A benign, bounded window does not justify regressing a load-bearing architectural invariant. Documented in `docs/runbooks/disaster-recovery.md` ("Pre-draft crash boundary") and drilled in `tests/test_publish.py::test_fresh_runner_completes_same_build_at_every_boundary`, whose assertions encode exactly this contract: the durably-recoverable (draft-onward) boundaries complete the same build_id, while the pre-draft and no-durable-journal boundaries refuse safely — never a partial pointer or a deleted draft.

**Re-raised & re-affirmed (round 6, 2026-07-23):** an external review again flagged that the three earliest boundaries (`staged_journal_pre_draft`, `draft_created_no_assets`, `partial_journal_upload`) "expect failure instead of completing the same build_id." **Re-affirmed owner-accepted:** their behavior is SAFE (nothing stranded / orphan draft preserved / no partial pointer), not a failure; making them complete-same-build_id requires the rejected DB-in-git regression above. Behavior and tests unchanged; contract language above made precise so it reads as by-design.

**Filesystem trust boundary (§14, owner-accepted — bounded by design).** Populus hardens **all untrusted-data-derived paths** — manifest/pointer/asset/journal/module names — via containment chokepoints (`resolve_within`/`archive_path`, `LocalDirBackend._safe_path`, `SnapshotClient._safe_under`) plus strict grammar (build_id `YYYYMMDD.N`, module `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`). It **additionally refuses symlinks at the specific base subdirs/files it OWNS AND CREATES** — `releases/`, `builds/`, `.staging/`, and the monitor's `pointer-tuple.json`/`failures` — as cheap, bounded tamper-detection (checked on the owned component with `is_symlink()`, before any write; never `.resolve()`-then-trust). It **treats the *configured* `data_repo` and monitor `state_dir` roots THEMSELVES as trusted operator inputs**: defending a symlinked configured-root (or a symlinked `$HOME`/parent above it) is **explicitly out of the §14 threat model** — that precondition already implies publisher-filesystem write access, at which point an attacker could edit code or the source DB directly. The check is bounded to the owned children by design and deliberately does **not** regress into infinite parent-directory chasing.
